Topics · Meaning and purpose

Is my work worship?

Prayer, life and death under God, and a verse from prayer to the market. When does daily work turn to God?

Part 1 of 3

﴿قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِى وَنُسُكِى وَمَحْيَاىَ وَمَمَاتِى لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allāh, Lord of the worlds.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:162

Translation

Preserve me, God, for I take refuge in you. My soul, you have said to Yahweh, “You are my Lord. Apart from you I have no good thing.”

Original · Hebrew

מִכְתָּ֥ם לְדָוִ֑ד שָֽׁמְרֵ֥נִי אֵ֝֗ל כִּֽי־חָסִ֥יתִי בָֽךְ׃ אָמַ֣רְתְּ לַֽ֭יהוָה אֲדֹנָ֣י אָ֑תָּה ט֝וֹבָתִ֗י בַּל־עָלֶֽיךָ׃

the Psalms · 16:1-2

World English Bible

If worship were limited to the hour of prayer, most of life would lie outside it. This verse counts: my prayer, my rites, my living, my dying, for God. Between prayer and death stands all of life: waking, working, eating, coming home. So the issue is less the kind of activity than its direction. What is turned toward God enters the list.

A question for you

Which word in the list surprises you most?

If you sayMy living.
ThenThen this Step starts there: where does your work stand under that word?
If you sayMy dying.
ThenOne who gives their death to God sees their life that way too. That thought is not rushed.
If you sayNone of them.
ThenPerhaps you already live this. The next part tests it in the market.

Part 2 of 3

﴿فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةُ فَٱنتَشِرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allāh, and remember Allāh often that you may succeed.

Quran · Al-Jumu'ah 62:10

Translation

Always rejoice. Pray without ceasing.

Original · Ancient Greek

πάντοτε χαίρετε, ἀδιαλείπτως προσεύχεσθε,

1 Thessalonians · 5:16-17

World English Bible

If work were the opposite of worship, leaving prayer for the market would be a step down. Yet the verse sends people out after prayer to spread through the land and seek God's bounty, and it adds: remember God often. The market does not take you out of remembrance. And a living is itself called God's bounty. Going out to work can extend the prayer, not abandon it.

A question for you

How far is your prayer from your work?

If you sayVery far.
ThenThen this verse is a short bridge you could try once.
If you sayClose some days, far on others.
ThenAn honest answer, and most people are like that.
If you sayI do not pray.
ThenThe verse still says something: that work is a seeking of a good not made by you alone. There is a question on this as well.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَقُلِ ٱعْمَلُوا۟ فَسَيَرَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۖ وَسَتُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَـٰلِمِ ٱلْغَيْبِ وَٱلشَّهَـٰدَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And say, "Do [as you will], for Allāh will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."

Quran · At-Tawbah 9:105

Translation

And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men,

Original · Ancient Greek

ὃ ἐὰν ποιῆτε, ἐκ ψυχῆς ἐργάζεσθε, ὡς τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις,

Colossians · 3:23

World English Bible

﴿إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ﴾

Translation of the meaning

But only seeking the face [i.e., acceptance] of his Lord, Most High.

Quran · Al-Layl 92:20

Translation

He also said to the one who had invited him, “When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back. But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind; and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν· Ὅταν ποιῇς ἄριστον ἢ δεῖπνον, μὴ φώνει τοὺς φίλους σου μηδὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου μηδὲ τοὺς συγγενεῖς σου μηδὲ γείτονας πλουσίους, μήποτε καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀντικαλέσωσίν σε καὶ γένηται ἀνταπόδομά σοι. ἀλλʼ ὅταν δοχὴν ποιῇς, κάλει πτωχούς, ἀναπείρους, χωλούς, τυφλούς· καὶ μακάριος ἔσῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνταποδοῦναί σοι, ἀνταποδοθήσεται γάρ σοι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῶν δικαίων.

the Gospel (Luke) · 14:12-14

World English Bible

When does work itself become worship? Fine work can be done for a wage, and there is no shame in that. But the first verse adds an observer: God will see your work. The second adds an aim: seeking the face of God. These two transform work: that it is seen, and that it is directed. Worship here does not require a new job. It requires knowing before whom you are working.

A question for you

What would bring your work closest to worship?

If you sayTo intend good by it.
ThenThat is what the verse calls seeking the face of your Lord.
If you sayTo do it well.
ThenDoing it well is one face of intention, and the verse says it is seen.
If you sayTo be fair with those I work with.
ThenA wide door, with a Step of its own on justice.

The same in the other books

Translation

I delight to do your will, my God. Yes, your law is within my heart.”

Original · Hebrew

לַֽעֲשֽׂוֹת־רְצוֹנְךָ֣ אֱלֹהַ֣י חָפָ֑צְתִּי וְ֝ת֥וֹרָתְךָ֗ בְּת֣וֹךְ מֵעָֽי׃

the Psalms · 40:8

World English Bible

Translation

Whether therefore you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.

Original · Ancient Greek

Εἴτε οὖν ἐσθίετε εἴτε πίνετε εἴτε τι ποιεῖτε, πάντα εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ ποιεῖτε.

1 Corinthians · 10:31

World English Bible

To a good man there is no evil, either in life or death. And if God supply not food, has He not, as a wise Commander, sounded the signal for retreat and nothing more? I obey, I follow—speaking good of my Commander, and praising His acts. For at His good pleasure I came; and I depart when it pleases Him; and while I was yet alive that was my work, to sing praises unto God!

Stoic writings · Golden Sayings 134

Epictetus, Golden Sayings (Crossley)

Your reflection

What is the smallest part of your work you could do tomorrow for the sake of God?
